relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT with a date caveat: the PDF is arXiv:math/0406276v1, DeTurck-Gluck, 'The Gauss linking integral on the 3-sphere and in hyperbolic 3-space', dated June 2004 on its own front matter; the registry records year 2008 (the journal publication) with this arXiv URL, so the join holds. BIB ORPHAN: a full-tree grep for the key returns zero hits outside folio/schema/references.ts - not a single .md, .lean, .ts, .py, .json or docs/ mention. This one is not previously recorded as uncited, unlike its sibling franecki-kapranov-1999. The paper gives explicit integral formulas for linking, twisting, writhing and helicity on S^3 and in H^3 that are isometry-invariant (geometric, not merely topological), derives them from a steady-state electrodynamics with an explicit Biot-Savart formula and Ampere's law, and obtains upper bounds for helicity and lower bounds for the first curl eigenvalue on subdomains. Note the front matter's own caveat: 'We give only a hint of the proofs.' The folio has live blocks in exactly this area - rem:helicity-physical, rem:townsend-biot-savart-strain, rem:vorticity-lower-bound-argument - which is why this is supporting rather than tangential. Corpus-grep run before proposing: docs/audits/, content/, computations/ and docs/coordination/ carry no citation of this work; the closest recorded reading is the komendarczyk2008 registry note on third-order helicity.

keyResults.statement: Explicit isometry-invariant integral formulas for linking, twisting, writhing and helicity in S^3 and H^3, with the Biot-Savart formula yielding upper bounds for helicity and lower bounds for the first eigenvalue of curl on subdomains.
keyResults.useForFolio: The hyperbolic-space version is the setting the framework actually works in; a helicity upper bound in H^3 is the natural comparison for the vorticity lower-bound argument, which currently argues in the Euclidean setting.

proposedActions.rationale: A registered reference giving helicity bounds and a Biot-Savart formula in hyperbolic 3-space is uncited while three fluid-dynamics remarks argue about helicity and Biot-Savart strain. Cite it where the ambient-geometry dependence of the helicity bound is discussed.
